plan: In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), there's no incentive to shade my bid. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks winning at a loss. With my value at $24, the optimal bid is exactly $24 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of opponents' strategies. This is because if I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding higher than my value only risks overpaying, while bidding lower only risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $9, I should bid exactly $9 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay only the second-highest bid if I win, bidding my actual value of $13 ensures I never overpay and maximizes expected profit regardless of what others bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions, and bidding higher risks winning at a loss. I'll bid exactly $13.
